chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever is poor, let him eat reasonably.' He said: 'That is a man who withholds himself from livelihood (to manage orphans' affairs), so there is no harm if he eats reasonably if he is managing their wealth for them. If the wealth is small, he should not eat anything from it.'
He said: I said, 'What is your view of the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And if you intermingle with them, then they are your brethren
He said: 'You take from their wealth an amount that suffices for them, and you take from your wealth an amount that suffices for you, then you spend it.'

I said, 'What is your view if they are orphans, young and old, and some of them have better clothing than others, and some eat more than others, and their wealth is together?' He said: 'As for the clothing, the cost of each person's clothing is upon him individually. As for the eating of food, make it all-inclusive, for the young are likely to eat as much as the old.'

key_terms.يَحْبِسُ نَفْسَهُ: withholds himself (from seeking independent livelihood to manage the estate)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a guardian eating from an orphan's wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Quranic verses on orphan guardianship, distinguishing between reasonable compensation for active management and the prohibition of self-enrichment when funds are scarce. It further refines the concept of 'intermingling' finances by mandating that the custodian's sustenance be drawn from their own resources while covering the orphans' needs from theirs, ensuring equitable treatment regardless of age or status differences within the group.
